newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Valenzuela sees '96 GDP growth at 4.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Valenzuela sees '96 GDP growth at 4.5 pct.

text.p: Mexico's gross domestic product likely will grow by at least 4.5 percent in 1996, Alejandro Valenzuela, the Finance Ministry's top spokesman, told a news conference on Wednesday.

Valenzuela also said the market is predicting that December 1996 inflation will be between 3.0 percent and 3.5 percent, and that the government "would not be surprised" to see January 1997 inflation of "around two percent."

"We are now seeing that (GDP growth) is entering 4.5 (percent) and possibly a little more as the year ends," Valenzuela said in his regular news conference, adding that the final result will be "much higher" than the three percent growth that the government predicted at the start of the year.
As for market predictions of December inflation, Valenzuela said "there is a range between three (percent) and 3.5 (percent)."

"This increase ... is due in its totality to the increases in prices that were agreed upon in the Alianza," he said, referring to the government, business and labor alliance also known as the Pacto that sets economic goals in November of each year.
But he said consumer prices are likely to slow their increase in January, adding that, "It would not be surprising to see inflation in January of around two percent."
